about.description:
Hi, I'm Pranav, an AI/ML Engineer and B.Tech Computer Science (Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning) graduate based in Hyderabad, India. I specialize in building end-to-end AI applications powered by Large Language Models, Generative AI, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and multi-agent systems.

My core toolkit includes Python, LangChain, LangGraph, and PyTorch, backed by full-stack expertise in the MERN/PERN stack - which lets me take an AI idea from a working model all the way to a deployed, production-ready application. My foundation in machine learning, deep learning, and NLP has been reinforced through certifications from Stanford University and DeepLearning.AI.
I'm passionate about developing intelligent, production-ready AI solutions and am actively looking for opportunities as a Full-Stack AI Engineer, AI Application Engineer, LLM Engineer, or Generative AI Engineer.

projects.title: AI Personal Agent Workspace
projects.description: Architected a full-stack, production-ready multi-agent AI productivity platform that unifies a conversational chat agent, task management, Gmail-based email intelligence, and RAG-powered code and document search behind a single JWT-authenticated interface with per-user data isolation and a custom glassmorphism UI.
bullets: Engineered a dual RAG pipeline using OpenAI's text-embedding-3-small and ChromaDB with two independent vector stores: one for GitHub repository intelligence (clones any public repo, chunks and embeds source files, and answers natural-language questions grounded in the codebase) and one for personal document Q&A supporting PDF and Markdown uploads.

Built an autonomous chat agent that parses every response as structured JSON to extract and save actionable tasks automatically, maintaining a rolling 5-message context window for coherent multi-turn conversations.
Integrated Gmail via IMAP SSL to fetch unread emails and used GPT to classify and convert them into priority-tagged tasks, distinguishing meeting invites and action items from routine newsletters.
Optimized API cost and latency through an in-memory query cache, fixed-size chunking strategy, and stateless JWT + bcrypt authentication with OAuth2PasswordBearer-compatible flow.

projects.title: Bigram Language Model
projects.description: Built a character-level bigram language model from scratch using PyTorch to generate unique, plausible-sounding names, implementing the full neural network pipeline manually to demonstrate a hands-on grasp of probabilistic sequence modeling rather than relying on pre-trained components or high-level libraries.
bullets: Implemented the complete training loop — one-hot character encoding, a single linear layer, softmax output, and negative log-likelihood loss with L2 regularization — trained via vanilla gradient descent over 1000 epochs.
Built a CLI supporting both training and inference modes, with model weights and character-to-index mappings persisted for reuse.
Achieved reproducible generation through seeded sampling, producing realistic new names from a learned character-transition distribution.

projects.title: Hand Gesture Volume Control
projects.description: Developed a real-time computer vision application that controls system audio volume using hand gestures, combining MediaPipe's hand landmark detection with OpenCV video processing and PyCaw for direct system-level audio control, enabling fully touchless volume adjustment.
bullets: Built a reusable HandDetector module on top of MediaPipe to identify and track hand landmarks in real time and render them on the live video feed.
Mapped the Euclidean distance between the thumb and index finger to the system volume range via interpolation, enabling smooth, low-latency gesture-driven control.
Displayed real-time FPS and volume level overlays on the video stream for immediate visual feedback.

courses.title: The Web Developer Bootcamp (PERN Stack)
courses.Takeaway: This is where I built my core engineering instincts. The course covers the full PERN stack end to end: HTML/CSS and JavaScript fundamentals, DOM manipulation, server-side development with Node.js and Express, RESTful API design, relational data modeling with PostgreSQL, authentication (sessions, JWT, password hashing with bcrypt), and deploying a working app to production. I built multiple CRUD applications from scratch - user auth flows, database-backed apps, and a capstone project wiring a React frontend to an Express/PostgreSQL backend. This foundation matters more than it might seem for AI work: an LLM-powered product is still, underneath, a full-stack application - APIs, databases, auth, and a frontend - with a model in the loop.

courses.title: React
courses.Takeaway: A focused, practical pass through modern React: components and JSX, hooks (useState, useEffect, and writing custom hooks), props vs. state, conditional rendering, list rendering, and client-side routing with React Router. This paired directly with the backend skills from the PERN bootcamp and gave me the frontend fluency I later used to build the Next.js interface for my AI Personal Agent Workspace project - the UI layer for chat interfaces, agent dashboards, and tool-triggered views that AI applications need.

courses.title: Machine Learning Specialization
courses.Takeaway: The theoretical backbone of everything I've built since. This specialization covers supervised learning (linear and logistic regression, gradient descent, regularization to control overfitting), neural networks built up from a single neuron to multi-layer architectures, decision trees and ensemble methods, unsupervised learning (k-means clustering, anomaly detection, dimensionality reduction), and an introduction to recommender systems and reinforcement learning. What this course gave me isn't just "which function to call" - it's the underlying math and intuition for why a model learns what it learns, which makes debugging and reasoning about model behavior far less of a black box.

courses.title: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
courses.Takeaway: The course that took me from "using" neural networks to actually understanding what's happening inside them. I built micrograd, a tiny autograd engine from scratch in pure Python, to understand backpropagation at the level of individual scalar operations. Then makemore, progressing from a bigram character-level model through MLPs, batch normalization, and a WaveNet-style architecture. The capstone was building GPT from scratch (nanoGPT) - implementing self-attention and multi-head attention by hand and writing a full transformer block - plus a deep dive into the GPT-2 tokenizer and byte-pair encoding. This is what demystified the LLMs I now build applications on top of; I'm not just calling an API, I understand the mechanics underneath it.

courses.title: PyTorch
courses.Takeaway: The practical, hands-on complement to the theory above - translating "I understand how a neural network works" into "I can build and train one in a production-grade framework." Covers tensors and tensor operations, autograd in PyTorch specifically, the standard training workflow (data → model → loss/optimizer → training loop), computer vision projects using CNNs and transfer learning with torchvision, building custom Dataset/DataLoader pipelines, and considerations for saving and deploying trained models. This is the framework fluency layer that connects ML theory and from-scratch understanding to actually shipping models.

courses.title: Introduction to LangChain
courses.Takeaway: Focused on the orchestration layer that sits between raw LLM API calls and a full production system: chains, prompt templates, structured output parsing, memory, and an introduction to LangGraph for building stateful, graph-based LLM workflows - nodes, edges, conditional routing, and cycles instead of linear chains. This is what makes it possible to move from "single prompt, single response" to multi-step, stateful LLM applications.

courses.title: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with LangChain
courses.Takeaway: An end-to-end walkthrough of building RAG pipelines: document loading, chunking strategies, generating embeddings, storing and querying vector databases, designing retrievers, and combining retrieval with generation, along with an introduction to evaluating RAG output quality. I applied this directly in my AI Personal Agent Workspace project, where I used ChromaDB as the vector store to ground the agent's responses in retrieved context rather than relying purely on the model's parametric knowledge.

courses.title: AI Agents Course
courses.Takeaway: Covers what actually makes an LLM call an "agent": reasoning combined with tool use and memory, the ReAct pattern, function/tool calling, and building agents with frameworks like smolagents, LlamaIndex, and LangGraph. Also covers multi-agent systems and the basics of agent evaluation and observability. This is the most directly relevant course to the AI Application / LLM Engineer roles I'm targeting - the shift from building single-turn chatbots to building autonomous, tool-using systems that can take multi-step actions.

courses.title: Rust
courses.Takeaway: I went through the official Rust Book to build systems-level intuition that JavaScript and Python don't force you to develop. Core topics: ownership and borrowing, the borrow checker, lifetimes, structs/enums and pattern matching, error handling with Result/Option instead of exceptions, and traits and generics. Rust's compile-time guarantees around memory safety (without a garbage collector) changed how I think about state and mutation even when I'm writing Python. It's also increasingly relevant to AI infrastructure - tokenizers, inference servers, and performance-critical ML tooling (e.g. Hugging Face's tokenizers, candle) are written in Rust.
